extraction.name: LongVid
extraction.description: A large-scale long video instruction-tuning dataset comprising 114,228 long videos and 3,444,849 question-answering pairs across five task types for diverse long video scenarios.
extraction.creator: Xinhao Li, Yi Wang, Jiashuo Yu, Xiangyu Zeng, Yuhan Zhu, Haian Huang, Jianfei Gao, Kunchang Li, Yinan He, Chenting Wang, Yu Qiao, Yali Wang, Limin Wang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: LongVid was constructed by leveraging existing datasets spanning movies, egocentric videos, news, interviews, how-to videos, and other in-the-wild long-duration videos. The authors generated dense event labels for each long video using existing short video captions, filtered consecutive segments that could be regrouped into long video sequences, directly used existing event-level annotations when available, extracted major events from captions using an LLM otherwise, and then constructed long video QA pairs from captions, event labels, and timestamps.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Existing datasets Ego4D, HowTo100M, HD-VILA, and MiraData, along with their associated captions and annotations such as Panda-70M, CosMo, Ego4D-HCap, HT-Step, and original MiraData captions.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset was curated by filtering consecutive short-video segments that could be regrouped into long video sequences, constructing event-label sequences with timestamps, directly using existing event-level annotations when available, extracting major events from captions using an LLM for other datasets, and constructing QA pairs from captions, event labels, and timestamps.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Consecutive segments were filtered and regrouped into long video sequences; dense event labels with timestamps were constructed from captions; for some datasets major events were extracted from captions using an LLM.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations consist of dense event labels and QA pairs. Event labels were derived either directly from existing high-quality event-level annotations or by extracting major events from captions using an LLM. QA pairs were then constructed from video captions, event labels, and timestamps, covering five tasks: video captioning, temporal grounding, event relation recognition, scene relation recognition, and video event counting.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For the Multi-Hop Needle-in-a-Video-Haystack benchmark, the paper discusses reducing information leakage by sourcing all images from MS-COCO and using its human-annotated captions and question-answer pairs, noting that even if a model memorized MS-COCO content, it would not help much in finding the needle. For LongVid construction, datasets with high-quality event-level annotations are directly used as event labels, while for others the major event is extracted from captions using an LLM.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes potential information leakage in prior long-video evaluation setups when images and questions similar to the needle may appear in training data; their new benchmark is designed to reduce such leakage.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Existing long-form video-text datasets lack the instruction-following paradigm of (video, instruction, answer) triplets crucial for multimodal reasoning. The paper also notes drawbacks of prior NIAH-Video evaluation: possible information leakage and insufficient assessment of reasoning ability.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: LongVid is used for long video instruction tuning and joint short-and-long video instruction tuning to train models for diverse long video scenarios and tasks including video captioning, temporal grounding, event relation recognition, scene relation recognition, and video event counting.
